Lung datasets: figures¶

In this notebook, we load each lung dataset (which has already been cell type annotated) and plot the UMAP projections with their appropriate cell type labels.

In [1]:

Palettes¶

In the figures, we use two types of palettes: 1) General palettes to label mouse IDs, sample IDs, age, etc. and 2) a cell-type specific palette that was created so that related cell types had similar colors. The latter is used to ease the comparison between equivalent cell types in different datasets.

In [2]:
# General palettes
safe = Safe_10.hex_colors
bold_and_vivid = Bold_10.hex_colors + Vivid_10.hex_colors
pastel = Pastel_10.hex_colors

dsets = ['angelidis', 'kimmel', 'tms_facs', 'tms_drop']
df_dsets = pd.DataFrame(index=dsets)

for dset in dsets:
    # Number of cells per category
    adata = eval(f'adata_{dset}')
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'total_cells'] = adata.shape[0]
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'young_cells'] = adata[adata.obs['age'] == 'Young'].shape[0]
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'old_cells'] = adata[adata.obs['age'] == 'Old'].shape[0]
    
    # Number of mice per category
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'total_mice'] = len(set(adata.obs['mouse']))
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'young_mice'] = len(set(adata[adata.obs['age'] == 'Young'].obs['mouse']))
    df_dsets.loc[dset, 'old_mice'] = len(set(adata[adata.obs['age'] == 'Old'].obs['mouse']))

UMAP projections¶

Two types of plots:

  • UMAP with legend in SVG
  • UMAP without legend in PNG (to create the panels)
In [19]:
def plot_umap(adata, var, color_dic, size):
    color = color=[color_dic[ct] for ct in adata.obs[var]]
    x, y = adata.obsm['X_umap'][:,0], adata.obsm['X_umap'][:,1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(5,5))
    ax.scatter(x, y, c=color, s=size)
    plt.legend(handler_map=color_dic)
    plt.axis('off')
    patchList = []
    for key in color_dic:
        data_key = mpatches.Patch(color=color_dic[key], label=key)
        patchList.append(data_key)
    plt.legend(handles=patchList, loc='center right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 1.0), ncol= 2)
In [20]:
def plot_umap_no_legend(adata, var, color_dic, size):
    color = color=[color_dic[ct] for ct in adata.obs[var]]
    x, y = adata.obsm['X_umap'][:,0], adata.obsm['X_umap'][:,1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(5,5))
    ax.scatter(x, y, c=color, s=size)
    plt.axis('off')

Cell type composition¶

In [38]:
def plot_stacked_barplot(df_curated, young, old, dset_name):
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(2, 5))

    series_labels = df_curated.index

    data_young = [df_curated.loc[ct, f'{young}_perc'].tolist() for ct in df_curated.index]
    data_old = [df_curated.loc[ct, f'{old}_perc'].tolist() for ct in df_curated.index]

    data = [[data_young[i], data_old[i]] for i in range(len(data_young))]
    category_labels = ['Young', 'Old']

    plot_stacked_bar(
        data, 
        series_labels, 
        category_labels=category_labels, 
        show_values=False, 
        value_format="{:.1f}",
        colors = [cell_type_colors[ct] for ct in df_curated.index],
        y_label="Cell type composition (%)"
    )
    handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
    plt.legend(handles[::-1], labels[::-1], bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1.0), loc='upper left', ncol=1)
    plt.title(dset_name)
    
#     plt.show()
In [39]:
def preprocess_cell_type_composition(path2input):
    """
    Some preprocessing is needed to remove very rare cell types (<1%) and put them together in a category
    named "Others". 
    """
    df_ct = pd.read_csv(path2input,index_col=0)
    df_ct.sort_index(axis=0, key=lambda index_lst: [ct_order[ct] for ct in index_lst], inplace=True)
    df_curated = df_ct[df_ct['Young_perc'] > 1]
    df_curated.loc['Others', :] = np.sum(df_ct[df_ct['Young_perc'] < 1], axis=0)
    return df_curated

def plot_violins_per_age(dist_df, name_dset):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(5, 7))
    
    median, mean, q25, q75 = [], [], [], []
    ages = ['Young', 'Old']
    for age in ages:
        median.append(np.median(dist_df[dist_df.age==age].mean_membership))
        mean.append(np.mean(dist_df[dist_df.age==age].mean_membership))
        q25.append(np.quantile(dist_df[dist_df.age==age].mean_membership, 0.25))
        q75.append(np.quantile(dist_df[dist_df.age==age].mean_membership, 0.75))

    
    ax.plot(ages, q25, '--', color='#C1C1C1', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.plot(ages, q75, '--', color='#C1C1C1', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.fill_between(ages, q25, q75, alpha=0.3, color='#C1C1C1')
    ax.plot(ages, median, color='#007BA7')
    sns.violinplot(data = dist_df, x= 'age', y='mean_membership', order=ages, ax=ax, color='#007BA7', s=0.5, jitter=0.25, alpha=0.6)
    ax.set_title(name_dset)
    ax.set_xlabel('Mean membership score')

Increase in noise vs cell type enrichment in old samples¶

In [8]:
def create_noise_df(distributions_df): 
    noise_df = pd.DataFrame(index=set(distributions_df.cell_type))
    
    for ct in noise_df.index:
        # Percentage of cells with a membership score < 0.8
        df_ct = distributions_df[distributions_df.cell_type == ct]
        noise_df.loc[ct, 'Young'] = df_ct[df_ct.mean_membership <= 0.8][df_ct.age == 'Young'].shape[0]/df_ct.shape[0]
        noise_df.loc[ct, 'Old'] = df_ct[df_ct.mean_membership <= 0.8][df_ct.age == 'Old'].shape[0]/df_ct.shape[0]

        # Median membership score
        df_young = distributions_df[((distributions_df.cell_type == ct) & (distributions_df.age == 'Young'))]
        df_old = distributions_df[((distributions_df.cell_type == ct) & (distributions_df.age == 'Old'))]
        noise_df.loc[ct, 'Young_median'] = df_young.mean_membership.median()
        noise_df.loc[ct, 'Old_median'] = df_old.mean_membership.median()
    noise_df.loc[:, 'Diff'] = noise_df.Old - noise_df.Young
    noise_df.loc[:, 'Diff_median'] = noise_df.Young_median - noise_df.Old_median
    noise_df.fillna(0, inplace=True) # If one ct if absent in one of the two categories, assume there is no
                                    # age-related difference in membership

    return noise_df

def create_enrichment_df(ct_per_age):
    ct_per_age.loc[:, 'odds_ratio'] = [1/x for x in ct_per_age.loc[:, 'odds.ratio']] #old/young instead of young/old
#     ct_per_age = ct_per_age[ct_per_age.Cell_type.isin(noise_df.index)]
#     ct_per_age.loc[noise_df.index, 'Noise_increase'] = noise_df.Diff
    return ct_per_age
In [9]:
def create_dfs(path2memberships, path2proportions):
    dis = pd.read_csv(path2memberships, index_col=0)
    noise = create_noise_df(dis)
    ct_per_age = pd.read_csv(path2proportions)
    ct_per_age = ct_per_age.set_index('Cell_type')
    cell_types = list(set(ct_per_age.index).intersection(set(noise.index)))
    noise = noise.loc[cell_types, :]
    ct_per_age = ct_per_age.loc[cell_types, :]
    ct_per_age = create_enrichment_df(ct_per_age)
    return noise, ct_per_age
In [10]:
def plot_noise_vs_enrichment(df_noise, df_enrichment, noise):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(6, 5))
    
    color = [cell_type_colors[ct] for ct in df_enrichment.index]
    
    if noise == 'median': 
        X = df_noise.Diff_median
        xlabel = 'Age-related increase in noise'
        
    elif noise == 'percentage':
        X = df_noise.Diff
        xlabel = 'Increase in % of noisy cells in old'
        
    Y = np.log10(df_enrichment.odds_ratio)
    size = 200 + 1500 * ((df_enrichment.prob - np.min(df_enrichment.prob))/(np.max(df_enrichment.prob) - np.min(df_enrichment.prob)))
    ax.scatter(x=X, y=Y, color=color, s=size, alpha=0.5)

    for x, y, ct in zip(X, Y, df_enrichment.index):
        ax.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct_numbers[ct], size=10)
#         ax.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct, size=10)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel('Old/young odds ratio')

    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

Broken Y axis¶

In the two TMS plots, as plasma cells are so much enriched, the range for the Y axis is too big, and most cell types appear in a much narrower range at the bottom of the plot. We will use a broken axis.

In [31]:
def plot_noise_vs_enrichment_broken_axis(df_noise, df_enrichment, noise):
        
    color = [cell_type_colors[ct] for ct in df_enrichment.index]
  

    if noise == 'median':
        X = df_noise.Diff_median

    elif noise == 'percentage':
        X = df_noise.Diff

    Y = np.log10(df_enrichment.odds_ratio)
    
    # Make size proportional to the number of cells of each category
    size = 200 + 1500 * ((df_enrichment.prob - np.min(df_enrichment.prob))/(np.max(df_enrichment.prob) - np.min(df_enrichment.prob)))
    
    
    outliers = df_enrichment[np.log10(df_enrichment.odds_ratio) > 5].index.tolist()
    if len(outliers) > 1: 
        print('Outliers:', outliers)
        # Outlier Y value: 
        y_out = np.max(np.log10(df_enrichment.odds_ratio[outliers]))
        # Maximum without outlier: 
        y_max_wo_out = np.log10(df_enrichment.drop(outliers).odds_ratio.max())
        # Minimum: 
        y_min = np.log10(df_enrichment.odds_ratio.min())
    
        ax_range = 0.2
        ax2_range = y_max_wo_out - y_min + 0.2

        # Plasma cells are so enriched in the two TMS datasets that we will need to break the
        # Y axis into two portions: the top portion (ax) will show the outlier (plasma cells) and 
        # the bottom portion (ax2) will show the rest of the cell types. 
        f, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True, figsize=(6, 5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [ax_range, ax2_range]})

        ax.set_ylim(y_out-0.1, y_out+0.1)  # Plasma cells only
        ax2.set_ylim(y_min-0.1, y_max_wo_out+0.1)  # most of the data

        ax.spines['bottom'].set_visible(False)
        ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
        ax.xaxis.tick_top()
        ax.tick_params(axis=u'both', which=u'both',length=0)
        ax.tick_params(labeltop=False)  # don't put tick labels at the top
        ax2.xaxis.tick_bottom()


        ax.scatter(x=X, y=Y, color=color, s=size, alpha=0.5)
        ax2.scatter(x=X, y=Y, color=color, s=size, alpha=0.5)

        for x, y, ct in zip(X, Y, df_enrichment.index):
            if ct not in outliers:
                ax2.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct_numbers[ct], size=10)
    #             ax2.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct, size=10)
            else: 
                ax.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct_numbers[ct], size=10)
    #             ax.text(x=x, y=y, s=ct, size=10)

        ax2.set_xlabel('Age-related increase in noise')
        ax2.set_ylabel('Old/young odds ratio')

        ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
        ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)

        ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

        d = .015  # how big to make the diagonal lines in axes coordinates
        kwargs = dict(transform=ax.transAxes, color='k', clip_on=False)
        ax.plot((-d, +d), (-d, +d), **kwargs)        # top-left diagonal

        r = ax_range/ax2_range #ratio between ax height and ax2 height
        kwargs.update(transform=ax2.transAxes)  # switch to the bottom axes
        ax2.plot((-d, +d), (1 - d*r, 1 + d*r), **kwargs)  # bottom-left diagonal
    
    else: 
        plot_noise_vs_enrichment(df_noise, df_enrichment, noise)

    plt.tight_layout()

Noise and enrichment rankings¶

In the previous plot, it was necessary to have both the noise and the enrichment for any given cell type. But in order to make the ranking figure, we do not need to have both values for the same cell type, because the enrichment and the noise are plotted separately.

We will therefore create new dataframes: noise_ranking and enrichment_ranking.

In [36]:
def increase_in_noise(path2memberships):
    # Noise
    distributions_df = pd.read_csv(path2memberships, index_col=0)
    df_noise = pd.DataFrame(index=set(distributions_df.cell_type))
    for ct in df_noise.index:
        # Median membership score
        df_young = distributions_df[((distributions_df.cell_type == ct) & (distributions_df.age == 'Young'))]
        df_old = distributions_df[((distributions_df.cell_type == ct) & (distributions_df.age == 'Old'))]
        df_noise.loc[ct, 'Young_median'] = df_young.mean_membership.median()
        df_noise.loc[ct, 'Old_median'] = df_old.mean_membership.median()
    df_noise.loc[:, 'Diff_median'] = df_noise.Young_median - df_noise.Old_median
#     noise_df.fillna(100, inplace=True)  # If one ct is missing in one of the two age groups, 
                                        # we will tag it with 100
    df_noise.drop(['Young_median', 'Old_median'], axis=1, inplace=True)
    return df_noise

def ct_enrichment(path2proportions):
    df_enrichment = pd.read_csv(path2proportions)
    df_enrichment = df_enrichment.set_index('Cell_type')
    df_enrichment.loc[:, 'odds_ratio'] = [1/x for x in df_enrichment.loc[:, 'odds.ratio']] #old/young instead of young/old
    return df_enrichment
In [37]:
def color_item(val):
    color = cell_type_colors[val]
    return 'color: %s' % color
In [38]:
def create_color_and_number_df(ranking, missing_ct):
    df_numbers = pd.DataFrame(index=ranking.index, columns=ranking.columns)
    df_colors = pd.DataFrame(index=ranking.index, columns=ranking.columns)
    for i in range(ranking.shape[0]):
        for j in range(ranking.shape[1]):
            ct = ranking.iloc[i][j]
            df_numbers.iloc[i, j] = ct_numbers[ct]
            dset = noise_ranking.iloc[:,j].name
            if ct not in missing_ct[dset]:
#             df_colors.iloc[i,j] = cell_type_colors[ct]
                df_colors.iloc[i, j] = ct_category_color[ct]
            else: 
                df_colors.iloc[i, j] = 'white'
    
    return df_colors, df_numbers

How many plasma cells/B cells are there in the TMS datasets?¶

The binomial GLM fitted on the two TMS datasets overestimates the enrichment of plasma cells, because very few plasma cells are detected. Therefore, the difference between old and young samples is huge.

Create noise and enrichment dataframes¶

In this dataframe we store the increase in noise associated to aging for each cell type in each dataset. Rows: cell types. Columns: datasets. Values: decrease in median membership score per cell type (young-old).

Create noise and enrichment ranking dataframes¶

In this dataframe we store all cell types, ordered according to their age-related increase in noise. The problem is that, since some cell types were absent in some of the datasets, when we sort the NaNs corresponding to those cell types, the order is not meaningful. Therefore, we need to keep track of the cell types that were absent (in amounts that were too small to run Scallop) in each dataset.

def plot_color_grid(df_colors, df_numbers, missing_ct):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=1, figsize=(3,7))
    for i in range(df_colors.shape[0]):
        for j in range(df_colors.shape[1]):
            dset = color_noise.iloc[:,j].name
            ax.hlines(-i, j-0.5, j+0.5, linewidth=13, color=df_colors.iloc[i, j])
            text = str(df_numbers.iloc[i][j])
            n_chars = len(text)
            if n_chars > 1:
                delta = 0.07
            else:
                delta = 0
            text_color = '#262626ff'
            if nb_celltypes[int(text)] in missing_ct[dset]: 
                text_color = 'white'
            ax.text(x=j-0.1 - delta, y=-i-0.3, s=text, size=10, color=text_color)
    ax.set_axis_off()
